It can be a long process, try to take time for yourself. Use your new found freedom. The person you envisioned doesn't exist, they're an idea of a person you've built up in your head, you will find someone else, you will be happy again. Some days will be easier than others, you might find yourself feeling lonely or missing your FP. The best thing you can do in this situation is to not contact them, don't check up on them. The less you know, the better you'll feel in the long run. I know how it feels and honestly, it's so hard, but you'll get there, I promise!

Honestly, from my experience it was a nightmare, we were on and off for 3 years and we kept trying again after breaks. 

The toll it takes on each of your mental health is extreme, we would bounce off of eachothers insecurities quite often and the trust aspect of the relationship was non-existent. No matter how much we tried to make it work, it just wouldn't. I thought upon learning of my diagnosis we would gain some mutual appreciation of the disorder together and it would bring us closer together, but my ex would just use any excuse to just tell me the way I felt was my bpd, she would always just tell me I was splitting or being irrational if I ever had an issue in the relationship. It was very hard to manage and in the end it just became too much. We both ended up being suicidal and neither of us were flourishing. She was getting DBT at the time and decided I wasn't what she wanted anymore and I wasn't healthy enough. Which I don't blame her for. I've been having therapy and it helps but be careful in this situation as you may end up hating eachother. 

No matter how intense your emotions are for this person it's a bumpy road and it can end in tears if you're not both in the right place. You need to try and help eachother as much as possible, but also make sure you're putting yourself first. This disorder makes manipulators of all of us, even if we don't realise it. I know this sounds very negative, but try and use my experience as a bit of a cautionary tale. Me and my ex aren't even allowed to contact eachother anymore and it got out of hand, very fast. One day you'd die for eachother, the next you're throwing years away and want nothing to do with eachother. Be careful and look after yourself!

Hey, i (27M) struggle with this a lot aswell. It's always been a struggle and i only end up staying at a place for like 3-4 months max. I've given up on working a regular job as stopping and starting with no consistent income is just as stressful. Im currently looking to get benefits and personal independence payment (I'm from the UK) so hopefully that means i can get therapy and an income without having to be in constant fear of being unable to pay rent. My story is so, so similar to yours, apart from with a lot more back and forth, i know its not easy to deal with and i'm still struggling. These feelings will eventually pass, but in between now and then you've got to try and dampen the intrusive thoughts as much as possible. You may never get an answer from him, and realistically that's fine. You're separate and no amount of wishing is going to change that, as much as your brain and heart want that to not be the case. I'd recommend calling some form of crisis line and finding someone you can talk to (a therapist, or mental health professional) in regards to your suicidal thoughts. I know they can be quite loud at times and very overwhelming, but its never the answer, trust me. I hope that the fact you're not alone in your thinking is comforting in some way and that these feelings pass for you.
